newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Grand Metropolitan jumps.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Grand Metropolitan jumps.

text.p: British consumer products company Grand Metropolitan rose strongly in New York on Monday, buoyed by its announced merger with drinks group Guinness Plc.

Traders said the market in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) was quiet, overshadowed by the Dow industrials' strong performance. The Dow was up 83 points to 7253 amid optimism ahead of a Federal Reserve rate-setting meeting May 20.
"The volumes are at the quietest non-holiday levels I can remember," a trader said. "The New York market is up so much -- that is where the interest is today."
Grand Metropolitan rose 4-3/4 to 38-7/8, a 12-month high, on volume that by late morning was three times normal daily levels.
The merger with Guinness will create the world's seventh-biggest food and drink company, worth more than $37 billion, and the world's leading spirits and wine company.
Grand Metropolitan's U.S. food interests, such as Burger King and Pillsbury, will be joined with Guinness' brewing operations.

French drinks and luxury goods company LVMH also rose 2-1/8 to 50-1/2 after a source close to the Grand Metropolitan-Guinness deal said LVMH would get about seven percent of the new combined company, GMG Brands.
LVMH has a 14.2 percent stake in Guinness.

Among Latin American shares, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose 1-3/8 to 125-7/8, helped by optimism for the selloff of cellular telephone bands and progress on a new telecommunications law.
Advancers led decliners 303 to 170 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.63 percent and volume just before midday was 34 million shares.
